body:
[2.8.6](https://appsecg.host/2.8):

> Verify that physical single-factor OTP generators can be revoked in case of theft or other loss. Ensure that revocation is immediately effective across logged in sessions, regardless of location.

Revoking a physical token?

comments.body: This is straight forward, you basically remove the seed on the server. It's built into most enterprise OTP admin consoles.
Do you think this only applies to TOTP or should it be widened to consider recovery codes, SMS OTP, push notifications, etc? @jmanico

This applies to any MFA. There is usually a "I lost my device" feature for most MFA solutions. But it's only for authentication and re-authentication, it's not a session issue so I'd drop the second sentence.  Closing out existing sessions is a different issue covered elsewhere.

_Verify that physical single-factor OTP generators can be revoked in case of theft or other loss. Ensure that revocation is immediately effective across logged in sessions, regardless of location._

Ok so I would propose:

"_Verify that any authentication factor (including physical devices) can be revoked in case of theft or other loss._"

> Ok so I would propose:
> 
> "_Verify that any authentication factor (including physical devices) can be revoked in case of theft or other loss._"

Perfect!
